title: How a two-wheeled robot steers
body: Many robots have no steering wheel. Each wheel has its own motor. The robot steers by spinning its wheels at different speeds. This is called differential drive.
The faster wheel covers more ground, so it swings round the slower one. Think of a marching band turning a corner: the outside row takes bigger steps. So the robot turns toward its slower wheel.
Equal speeds drive straight. The bigger the gap between the two speeds, the tighter the turn. One wheel forward and one backward spins the robot on the spot.
equation: turn rate = (right speed − left speed) ÷ wheel spacing
realWorld: Many classroom robots and robot vacuum cleaners steer this way, with no steering wheel at all.
sources: Columbia University CS W4733 notes, Differential Drive Robots (after Dudek & Jenkin, Computational Principles of Mobile Robotics). https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~allen/F17/NOTES/icckinematics.pdf
